tasks.title: Event Bus: TypeScript type definitions
tasks.description: Create scripts/lib/event-bus-types.ts — TypeScript-only type definitions for the Supabase Realtime event bus (v16 section 10E). No runtime code, no imports from Node or Supabase — pure TypeScript type declarations only. Define these event namespaces as string literal unions: TaskEventType = 'task.queued' | 'task.started' | 'task.completed' | 'task.failed' | 'task.rejected'; AgentEventType = 'agent.available' | 'agent.busy' | 'agent.degraded'; DataEventType = 'data.research.complete' | 'data.frame.extracted' | 'data.caption.generated'; InterruptEventType = 'interrupt.plumber.alert' | 'interrupt.budget.warning' | 'interrupt.budget.freeze'; SystemEventType = 'system.sprint.started' | 'system.sprint.completed' | 'system.heartbeat'. Export: KognaiEventType = union of all above; BaseEvent interface with {event_type: KognaiEventType; agent_id: string; sprint: string; timestamp: string; payload: Record<string, unknown>}; specific payload interfaces (TaskEventPayload with task_id, title, status, costUsdc?; BudgetEventPayload with burnPct, spentUsdc, budgetUsdc; SprintEventPayload with sprint, taskCount, completedCount); KognaiEvent as discriminated union by event_type using the payload interfaces where applicable. Also export type guard functions as type predicates: isTaskEvent(e: KognaiEvent): e is TaskEvent; isInterruptEvent(e: KognaiEvent): e is InterruptEvent; isSystemEvent(e: KognaiEvent): e is SystemEvent. Keep file under 120 lines.

tasks.title: Event Bus: Publisher module
tasks.description: Create scripts/lib/event-bus-publisher.ts — publishes KognaiEvents to Supabase via REST (no Supabase SDK, use built-in https module). Import KognaiEvent, KognaiEventType, TaskEventPayload, BudgetEventPayload, SprintEventPayload from './event-bus-types'. Config: reads SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY from process.env. If either is missing, log one warning to stderr on first publish attempt and no-op silently thereafter — never throw. Core function: async publishEvent(event: KognaiEvent): Promise<void> — HTTP POST to {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/kognai_events with headers {apikey: SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, Authorization: 'Bearer ' + SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, Content-Type: 'application/json', Prefer: 'return=minimal'}. Typed convenience wrappers (all call publishEvent internally): publishTaskStarted(agentId: string, sprint: string, taskId: string, title: string): Promise<void>; publishTaskCompleted(agentId: string, sprint: string, taskId: string, title: string, costUsdc: number): Promise<void>; publishTaskFailed(agentId: string, sprint: string, taskId: string, title: string, reason: string): Promise<void>; publishBudgetWarning(sprint: string, burnPct: number, spentUsdc: number, budgetUsdc: number): Promise<void>; publishBudgetFreeze(sprint: string, burnPct: number): Promise<void>; publishSprintStarted(sprint: string, taskCount: number): Promise<void>; publishSprintCompleted(sprint: string, taskCount: number, completedCount: number): Promise<void>. Use import * as https from 'https' (NOT import https from 'https'). Keep timeout at 5000ms — never block task execution. Export all functions.

issues.description: SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY are read at module load time (top-level const). If env vars are set after module import (e.g., in tests), the values will be stale. Reading from process.env inside checkConfig() would be more robust.

publishBudgetWarning, publishBudgetFreeze, publishSprintStarted, publishSprintCompleted hardcode agent_id as 'bloomberg'. The spec does not specify this value for non-task events, so it may be intentional, but it is worth confirming.

Payload objects are constructed inline without strict type validation against TaskEventPayload, BudgetEventPayload, SprintEventPayload. Works at runtime but loses compile-time safety. Consider casting or using type-safe constructors.

tasks.title: Event Bus: Listener module
tasks.description: Create scripts/lib/event-bus-listener.ts — polls Supabase REST for new KognaiEvents and delivers them to handlers. No Supabase Realtime SDK (use polling for simplicity). Import KognaiEvent, KognaiEventType from './event-bus-types'. Config: reads SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY from process.env. Graceful no-op if missing. Core: maintain an in-memory ring buffer (last 500 events). Export: subscribeToEvents(filter: { event_types?: KognaiEventType[]; agent_id?: string; sprint?: string }, handler: (event: KognaiEvent) => void): () => void — starts polling Supabase every 30s (GET /rest/v1/kognai_events?order=inserted_at.desc&limit=20), filters results, calls handler for each new event not already seen (track by inserted_at + event_type). Returns unsubscribe function that stops the interval. getEventLog(): readonly KognaiEvent[] — returns ring buffer contents. getActiveSubscriptionCount(): number. Use import * as https from 'https'. All HTTP calls wrapped in try/catch — polling failures are logged and retried on next tick, never throws. Keep file under 100 lines.

issues.description: The seenEvents Set is global and never pruned. Over time it will grow unboundedly, causing a memory leak. It should be bounded (e.g., capped at RING_BUFFER_SIZE entries or tied to the ring buffer).
File is approximately 120 lines, slightly over the spec's 100-line limit. Not a functional issue but violates the stated constraint.
Polling errors in fetchEvents are silently swallowed (resolve([])) rather than logged. The spec says 'polling failures are logged and retried on next tick' — the log step is missing.
The interval callback creates a new anonymous object literal for the subscription reference instead of using the stored subscription from the map, which is harmless but slightly redundant.
URL construction uses new URL() which may fail if SUPABASE_URL contains non-standard HTTPS ports or malformed URLs. Should wrap in try/catch or validate URL format.
